title: Melange: Cost Efficient Large Language Model Serving by Exploiting GPU Heterogeneity
technique: offline GPU-type allocation framework: workload slices bin-packed onto heterogeneous GPUs via ILP using profiled throughput under a TPOT SLO

optimized_metrics.evidence: Melange's objective is to choose a GPU allocation for the service workload that minimizes cost.
As in prior work [19, 58, 51], we use the average Time Per Output Token (TPOT) as our SLO. TPOT is determined by dividing request latency by the number of generated tokens.
the selected allocations successfully attain TPOT SLO for over 99.5% of requests

headline_claim.text: Compared to using only a single GPU type, Melange reduces deployment costs by up to 77% in conversational settings, 33% in document-based settings, and 51% in a mixed setting.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: TPOT is determined by dividing request latency by the number of generated tokens.
metric_definitions.notes: this is normalized latency (includes TTFT and queueing), i.e. NORM_LAT in the survey vocabulary, not decode-only TPOT; used as the SLO

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We use tokens per dollar (T/$) to measure GPU cost efficiency, calculated by summing input and output tokens and dividing the total by the GPU's on-demand rental cost for a given time period.
metric_definitions.notes: input+output tokens at highest saturation for which TPOT still meets SLO

slo_spec: average TPOT SLO of 40 ms (swift) or 120 ms (relaxed), chosen above human reading speed; attainment validated at >99.5% (40ms) and >99.95% (120ms)
load_regime: offline provisioning for a given request-rate/size distribution; request-rate sweep per dataset; low/high rate periods considered
tradeoff_acknowledged: tighter SLO shifts cost-efficient choice to expensive GPUs (A100/H100) and reduces savings
hardware: L4, A10G, A100-80G, H100 (cloud on-demand prices)
extractor_notes: Not a latency-optimization paper: cost is the single objective; latency enters only as constraint (mean TPOT as defined, which is latency/length, not decode-only). Models list not fully verified for all experiments.
